readout_other: Extracellular field potentials (fiber volley, dendritic potential, orthodromic and antidromic population spikes) in dentate gyrus; tissue temperature by thermocouple
direction_notes: Fiber volley and orthodromic population spike were depressed, the dendritic field potential was enhanced and the antidromic spike was little changed during 5-min exposures.
safety_notes: Cavitation was judged unlikely: no bubbles seen under the microscope and most responses recovered; tissue temperature rose 1.4 C on average.

exposures.label: 500 kHz pulsed focused ultrasound, rat hippocampal slice dentate gyrus

target.label: dentate gyrus region of the hippocampal slice

timing.protocol_description: The transducer was driven by 100-ns-wide square spikes at a pulse repetition rate of 200 kHz, giving acoustic pulses only a few cycles long; voltage was ramped to the operating level within 5 s. Slices were exposed for 5 min, allowed to recover 5-10 min, then exposed for another 5 min.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The transducer (Harisonic 18-0016-P, Staveley Sensors, Inc., East Hartford, CT, USA) had a center frequency of 500 kHz and a focal length of 7.6 cm.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.ispta_w_cm2: Folding in conservative estimates for systematic errors, these measurements yield $\mathrm { I _ { S P T A } }$ between 40 and 110 W/cm<sup>2</sup>.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: The amplifier was in turn driven by 100-ns-wide square spikes with pulse repetition rate of 200 kHz generated by a pulse/function generator (model 8116A, Hewlett-Packard, Palo Alto, CA, USA).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: When the evoked response stabilized to within 65% for at least 10 min, the tissue was exposed to focused, pulsed ultrasound for 5 min.

flags.reason: ISPTA estimated at low voltage by reciprocity calibration and calibrated hydrophone with transducer in a water tank, then extrapolated to the operating voltage; stated as a range with conservative systematic-error allowance.
Acoustic pulse described only as 'a few cycles in duration'; no numeric value, so not recorded. The 100 ns figure is the electrical drive spike.
PRF of 200 kHz is stated in the text (selected to fire the next pulse immediately after ring-down).
Number of rats not stated; 4 to 6 slices per experimental set and 6 slices for temperature work, overlap between sets unknown.
Protocol does not fit the four timing numbers: very short pulses at 200 kHz PRF with no stated pulse duration or duty cycle.
